title: On Conducting the choir without a score
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：conduct　|　正文 356 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 conduct 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1992 the keeper ① conducted the choir without a score without a word of thanks, and every traveller in the tower said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the keeper ② conducts the choir without a score at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ conduct the choir without a score at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ conducted the choir without a score before — a line in the calendar for January 1986 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Conducting the choir without a score without a word of thanks, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ conduct the whole inquiry in ten days at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Conduct the whole inquiry in ten days at once and never mention it again.

By 1999 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the calendar, and a new traveller from the next tower ⑧ conducts the whole inquiry in ten days without a word of thanks every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stair, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ conducted the choir without a score again when nobody else would.

⑩ To conduct the choir without a score, my mother said in 2004, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the tower remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the tower forgets, somebody conducts the choir without a score at once again and somebody must conduct the choir without a score without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 指挥（一般过去式 conducted the choir without a score：1992 年守夜人头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 指挥（一般现在 conducts the choir without a score：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 指挥（不定式 to conduct the choir without a score：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 指挥（过去完成时 had conducted the choir without a score：1986 年一月的年历上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 指挥（动名词 conducting the choir without a score 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 进行（conduct the whole inquiry in ten days：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去进行十天里做完整个调查）
G. v. 进行（conduct the whole inquiry in ten days：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 指挥（后段两处：新来的过路人照例 conducts the whole inquiry in ten days，而母亲又一次 conducted the choir without a score）

conduct 意为“指挥”，年历里 一月 那行字说明早在 1999 年之前就有人指挥过，故用过去完成时 had conducted。
conduct 意为“指挥”，守夜人说“指挥不看谱指挥那个唱诗班这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 conducting the choir without a score 作主语。
conduct 意为“进行”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去进行十天里做完整个调查”，should ever 之后用原形 conduct the whole inquiry in ten days。
conduct 意为“进行”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻进行十天里做完整个调查（conduct the whole inquiry in ten days at once），以后再也不要提起。
conduct 意为“指挥”，新来的过路人每个年头都照例进行十天里做完整个调查，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 conducts。

conduct 意为“指挥”，结尾那句是母亲 2004 年的话：要指挥不看谱指挥那个唱诗班，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和钟楼记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 conduct 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1992 the keeper conducted the choir without a score without a word of thanks, and nobody in the tower forgot it.
Even now the keeper conducts the choir without a score at once whenever the tower asks.
Conducting the choir without a score without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever conduct the whole inquiry in ten days at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next tower conducts the whole inquiry in ten days without a word of thanks every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother conducted the choir without a score again, and the tower remembered that half.
